title: National Rapid Mathematics
subject: Mathematics
description: The ExamForge Rapid Mathematics Competition is an exciting academic challenge designed to test participants' mathematical knowledge, speed, accuracy, and problem-solving abilities. It provides students with an opportunity to put their mathematical skills to the test in a competitive and engaging environment, where every second counts and every correct answer brings them closer to victory.

questions.question: Find the area of this triangle.
questions.explanation:
The area of a triangle is A = 12 × base × height.

Here the base is 8 units and the perpendicular height is 7 units (shown by the broken line), so A = 12 × 8 × 7 = 28 square units.

• Option B (56) comes from forgetting the factor of 12 and simply multiplying 8 × 7.
• Option C (15) comes from adding the base and the height instead of multiplying.
• Option D (24) does not follow from the given dimensions at all.

questions.question: How many times will this wheel rotate to reach from point A to point B?
questions.explanation:
The distance a wheel covers in one complete rotation is equal to its circumference.

Circumference C = 2πr

Using π = 227:

C = 2 × 227 × 7 = 44 cm

The number of rotations is the total distance divided by the circumference:

Rotations = 13244 = 3 times.

questions.question: If it takes 5 minutes for one towel to dry, how long will it take seven towels to dry if they are spread on a rope?
questions.explanation:
Drying time depends on environmental conditions (like sun and wind) and exposure, not on the total number of items, as long as they are spread out.

Because the seven towels are hung on the rope simultaneously, they dry in parallel. Therefore, they will all take the same amount of time as a single towel.

• Option A (35 minutes) is a common trap; it comes from multiplying 5 minutes × 7 towels, which only applies if they were dried one after the other.
• Options C and D are random incorrect calculations.

The correct answer is 5 minutes.

questions.question: If the current time is <kbd style='font-size: 1.4em; font-weight: 900; padding: 4px 10px; background: rgba(128,128,128,0.2); border-bottom: 3px solid currentColor;'>11:45 PM</kbd> on a Wednesday, what will be the exact day and time exactly 47 hours from now?
options: Friday, <kbd style='font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 900; padding: 2px 6px; background: rgba(128,128,128,0.2); border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor;'>10:45 PM</kbd>
Friday, <kbd style='font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 900; padding: 2px 6px; background: rgba(128,128,128,0.2); border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor;'>11:45 PM</kbd>
Thursday, <kbd style='font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 900; padding: 2px 6px; background: rgba(128,128,128,0.2); border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor;'>10:45 PM</kbd>
Saturday, <kbd style='font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 900; padding: 2px 6px; background: rgba(128,128,128,0.2); border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor;'>10:45 AM</kbd>
questions.explanation:
To solve this, it helps to break the 47 hours into a full day (24 hours) plus the remaining hours.

47 hours = 24 hours + 23 hours.

Step 1: Add 24 hours
Adding exactly 24 hours brings us to the exact same time on the next day.
Wednesday 11:45 PM + 24 hours = Thursday 11:45 PM.

Step 2: Add the remaining 23 hours
Start at Thursday 11:45 PM.
• Adding 1 hour brings us to Friday 12:45 AM.
• We still have 22 hours left to add (23 − 1 = 22).
• Friday 12:45 AM + 22 hours = Friday 10:45 PM.

The correct answer is Friday, 10:45 PM.

• Option B is a trap for those who forget to add the 23 hours after the first 24 hours.
• Option C is a trap for those who miscount the days.
• Option D is a trap for those who add instead of subtract when crossing over the 12-hour mark.

questions.question: The shape below is drawn with straight lines only, and all its angles are right angles. Calculate the perimeter of the shape.
questions.explanation:
To find the perimeter, we must add up the lengths of all the outside edges. First, we need to deduce the length of the missing bottom inner edge.

Step 1: Find the missing inner horizontal length
The total width at the bottom is 10 cm. The top of the shape is divided into three parts: the left top edge (2 cm), the inner gap (unknown), and the right top edge (2 cm).

Because the shape is formed by straight vertical and horizontal lines, the inner gap width equals the inner bottom edge width.
Inner width = 10 cm − 2 cm − 2 cm = 6 cm.

Step 2: Add all the outer sides
• Left vertical edge: 12 cm
• Bottom horizontal edge: 10 cm
• Right vertical edge: 12 cm
• Top-right horizontal edge: 2 cm
• Inner-right vertical edge: 4 cm
• Inner-bottom horizontal edge: 6 cm
• Inner-left vertical edge: 4 cm
• Top-left horizontal edge: 2 cm

Perimeter = 12 + 10 + 12 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 2 = 52 cm.

questions.question: A ladder leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 4 meters away from the base of the wall. If the ladder makes an angle of 60° with the ground, what is the length of the ladder?
questions.explanation:
Because the wall is vertical, the ladder, the wall, and the ground form a right-angled triangle.

The distance from the wall (4 m) is the side adjacent to the 60° angle. The ladder (x) is the hypotenuse.

Using the cosine ratio:
cos(θ) = adjacenthypotenuse

cos(60°) = 4x

We know that cos(60°) = 12.

12 = 4x

Cross-multiply:
x = 4 × 2 = 8 m.

questions.question:
The table below shows the marks scored by a group of students in a mathematics test.

Mark (x)TallyFrequency (f)
4||||5
6|||| |||8
8||2
10||||5

What is the mean mark of the data set?
questions.explanation:
To find the mean from a frequency table, we use the formula:

Mean = Sum of (f × x)Sum of f

First, we calculate the (f × x) for each row and find the totals:
• For x = 4: 5 × 4 = 20
• For x = 6: 8 × 6 = 48
• For x = 8: 2 × 8 = 16
• For x = 10: 5 × 10 = 50

Sum of frequencies (Sum of f) = 5 + 8 + 2 + 5 = 20
Sum of (f × x) = 20 + 48 + 16 + 50 = 134

Now, substitute these values into the formula:

Mean = 13420 = 6.7

The correct answer is 6.7.

questions.question:
Solve the following simultaneous equations to find the values of x and y:2x + y = 11
x − y = 1
questions.explanation:
We can solve this system using the elimination method by adding the two equations together to eliminate y.

Step 1: Add the equations
2x + y = 11
x − y = 1
(2x + y) + (x − y) = 11 + 1
3x = 12
x = 4

Step 2: Substitute x into the second equation
x − y = 1
4 − y = 1
y = 4 − 1
y = 3

So the solution is x = 4 and y = 3.

questions.question: The diagram above shows two concentric circles. The radius of the larger circle is 14 cm and the radius of the smaller circle is 7 cm. Calculate the area of the shaded portion. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
The shaded portion is an annulus (a ring shape). To find its area, subtract the area of the smaller circle from the area of the larger circle.

Step 1: Area of the larger circle
Area = πR² = 227 × 14² = 227 × 196 = 22 × 28 = 616 cm²

Step 2: Area of the smaller circle
Area = πr² = 227 × 7² = 227 × 49 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm²

Step 3: Area of the shaded portion
Area = (Area of larger circle) − (Area of smaller circle)
Area = 616 − 154 = 462 cm².

Alternatively, you can use the formula: Area = π(R² − r²) = 227 × (14² − 7²) = 227 × (196 − 49) = 227 × 147 = 22 × 21 = 462 cm².

questions.question: Which notation represents the shaded region in the Venn diagram?
questions.explanation:
The shaded region includes the entire universal set EXCEPT for the inside of Set B.

Notice that the only unshaded part is the right side of Set B (the part of B that does not overlap with A).

• Option A (A ∪ B) is incorrect because it would include the inside of Set B.
• Option B (A ∩ B) is incorrect because it represents only the overlapping intersection.
• Option D (A') is incorrect because it represents everything outside Set A, which is not what is shaded here.

Because the shaded area represents everything that is not in Set B, the correct notation is B'.

questions.question: The Venn diagram above shows the number of students who offer three subjects: A, B, and C. How many students offer exactly two of the three subjects?
questions.explanation:
To find the number of students who offer exactly two subjects, we must look only at the regions where two circles overlap but the third does not.

These regions are:
• A and B only = 4
• A and C only = 3
• B and C only = 6

Adding these together:
4 + 3 + 6 = 13 students.

• Option C (21) is a trap for those who include the center intersection (2). 13 + 2 = 15, or adding 8 (A only) gives 21.
• Option D (38) is the total number of students who offer at least one subject (the union).
• Option A (15) is the number of students who offer at least two subjects (4 + 3 + 6 + 2 = 15).

questions.question: Look at the numbers above. How many different 6-digit even numbers can be formed using all these digits without repetition?
questions.explanation:
To form an even number, the digit in the units (last) place must be an even number.

Step 1: Choose the last digit
The available even digits are 2, 4, and 6. Therefore, there are 3 choices for the last digit.

Step 2: Arrange the remaining digits
Once the last digit is chosen, there are 5 digits left to fill the first five positions. The number of ways to arrange these remaining 5 digits is 5 factorial (5!).

5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 ways.

Step 3: Calculate the total combinations
Total = (Choices for last digit) × (Arrangements for remaining digits)
Total = 3 × 120 = 360 ways.

• Option A (120) is the number of ways if the last digit was fixed to just one even number (e.g., just ending in 2).
• Option D (720) is the total number of 6-digit numbers that can be formed with no restrictions (6! = 720).

questions.question: Based on the two diagrams above, what is the height of the table?
questions.explanation:
Let the height of the table be T, the flask be F, and the box be B.

From the first diagram, the distance from the top of the flask to the top of the box is 150 cm:
Equation 1: T + F − B = 150

From the second diagram, the distance from the top of the box to the top of the flask is 110 cm:
Equation 2: T + B − F = 110

To find the height of the table, add both equations together. Notice that the +F and −F cancel out, and the −B and +B cancel out:
(T + F − B) + (T + B − F) = 150 + 110
2T = 260

Divide by 2:
T = 130 cm

• Option A (110 cm) is the height from the second diagram.
• Option C (150 cm) is the height from the first diagram.
• Option D (260 cm) is the trap answer you get if you forget to divide by 2 at the end.

questions.question: The Venn diagram above shows the number of students who study three subjects: Physics (P), Chemistry (C), and Biology (B). How many students study exactly two of the three subjects?
questions.explanation:
To find the number of students who study exactly two subjects, we must look only at the regions where two circles overlap but the third does not.

These regions are:
• Physics and Chemistry only = 5
• Physics and Biology only = 3
• Chemistry and Biology only = 4

Adding these together:
5 + 3 + 4 = 12 students.

• Option B (14) is a trap for those who include the center intersection (2). 12 + 2 = 14. (Adding the center gives you those who study at least two subjects).
• Option C (18) is a trap for those who add up all the overlapping regions completely, counting the center multiple times: (5+2) + (3+2) + (4+2) = 7 + 5 + 6 = 18.
• Option D (24) is simply the sum of all the numbers inside the three circles.
